newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CHH posts slight gain on better outlook.
newsitem.headline: CHH posts slight gain on better outlook.

text.p: Shares in Carter Holt Harvey Ltd (CHH) firmed six cents to NZ$3.29 after reporting a higher-than- expected annual result for the year to March.
CHH earlier reported a net profit of NZ$251 million, which was down 45 percent on the previous year's.
The decline was caused entirely by a price slump in almost all the areas CHH is involved in.
Analysts, who had been expecting around NZ$235-240 million, said there was a higher-than-expected monetary adjustment between the Chilean peso and the New Zealand dollar.

"The market seems to like the result," First NZ Capital broker Jim Patterson said. Approval was based on progress in CHH's cost containment programme and comments that suggested the pulp price recession had troughed, he said.
CHH has an indirect holding of just over 30 percent in Chilean forestry, fishing and petroluem company Copec.

"The operating result was a little lower than we expected, although there were continued one-off accounting adjustments in the building division, more than offset by a higher monetary adjustment through Copec," Steve Cozens at First NZ Capital said.
CHH and analysts said there appeared signs that the outlook for pulp and paper may be looking up, but much would depend on the pace of the recovery.
"Clearly global growth and pulp and paper demand is relatively robust, but the real problem is with excess supply," Cozens said.
John Cairns at Cavill White Securities said that while the result was an improvement on expectations, he did not expect to see much share price movement as a result.
However, he said, it did appear the worst may be over for CHH, which is jsut over half owned by International Paper.
